item.subject: science
item.stem: Meena collects a few drops of water from a pond near her school in Jaipur. To her unaided eye, the water looks clear with nothing living in it. Under a foldscope, she sees many tiny moving specks that she could not see before. What should Meena conclude about these tiny moving specks?

options.A: They are not living beings, because clear pond water cannot contain any organisms.
options.B: They are small dust particles, because anything invisible to the unaided eye must be nonliving.
options.C: They are microorganisms, because they are tiny living beings that can only be seen with magnification.
options.D: They are large insects, because only insects can live in pond water.
